The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO, Air Transport Division, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars Pan American World Airways, Inc., or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10811 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10811_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10811_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_baa6c6b760.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated June 15, 1959 and a letter of transmittal dated Washington, D.C., June 12, 1959; the board states that the parties agreed to extend the time for the report to June 15, 1959. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking June 15, 1959 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on June 15, 1959 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to July 15, 1959 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order.
